new.n: Old rope maker's missing savings, half-acre homestead south of Kenosha
new.pl: Half-acre homestead lot on the E side of the old N-S road through the NE1/4 of sec 7 T1N R23E, south side of Kenosha (probate sale description, 1896)
new.v: About $300 in recent payments plus years of savings (rumored)
new.st: An eccentric old rope maker who lived alone on a half-acre lot south of Kenosha was taken to the state asylum in fall 1895 and died there. He had lately been paid about $300 by Kenosha people and had a name for being miserly, but none of it had gone into a bank. His guardian, a neighbouring farmer, planned a systematic search of the house and grounds after the funeral. No find was reported, and the estate came to only $15 in goods plus the lot, sold for $225 in May 1896, all spent on costs. Whether anything was hidden is unproven.
new.t: The lot is now inside the Kenosha city area and likely built over: look only unless an open yard survives, and then only with permission. The old road is probably today's main N-S road through that quarter section.
src: Kenosha Co WI probate case 2133, report of sale 23 May 1896 and final account 18 Sep 1896 (Wisconsin Wills and Probate, Ancestry, PC (b)); research/ancestry/hank-kenosha.md
new.warn: Urban or suburban lot: look only; private.
pinev: Probate sale description: half acre, E side of the traveled road, NE1/4 sec 7 T1N R23E, checked against BLM PLSS (T1N R23E sec 7 = 42.551-42.566, just S of the 1895 city); r400 covers the quarter's road frontage
One local source for the hidden money; probate shows nothing found
